title: Watch Configurator with Strap Swap & Particle Effects
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with a Three.js-based interactive watch configurator featuring strap swapping with particle effects. Load the 3D model 'PrimaryIonDrive.glb' using GLTFLoader from a CDN (use unpkg or jsdelivr for Three.js r152+). This model represents the watch body.

SCENE SETUP:
- Set up a Three.js scene with a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 1.5, 3.5) looking at the origin.
- Add an OrbitControls for camera rotation (damping enabled).
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.5) and a directional light at (3, 5, 3) with intensity 1.2 and castShadow=true.
- Add a second point light at (-2, 2, -1) with intensity 0.6 for rim lighting.
- Background: gradient-like dark scene using scene.background = new THREE.Color(0x1a1a2e).
- Add a subtle circular platform (CylinderGeometry, radius 1.5, height 0.05) beneath the watch, metallic dark material.
- Load 'PrimaryIonDrive.glb' and center it at origin. Scale it so it fits roughly within a 1.5 unit bounding sphere. This is the watch body.

STRAP SYSTEM:
- Create 4 interchangeable strap options rendered as elongated rounded box geometries (BoxGeometry with slight modifications) attached above and below the watch body (y-offset ±0.4). Each strap is a pair of top/bottom pieces.
- Strap options: 'leather' (brown 0x8B4513), 'metal' (silver 0xC0C0C0, metalness 0.9), 'rubber' (black 0x222222, roughness 0.8), 'nato' (olive green 0x556B2F).
- Default strap: 'leather' (index 0).
- When swapping straps, the old strap fades out (opacity 0->remove) and the new strap fades in (opacity 0->1 over 0.5s), with a particle burst effect at the strap attachment points.

PARTICLE EFFECTS:
- Create a particle system using THREE.Points with BufferGeometry (200 particles).
- Particles are hidden by default. When a strap swap occurs, particles spawn at the strap attachment points, burst outward with random velocities, and fade out over 1.5 seconds.
- Particle color should match the NEW strap color.
- Track particle system active state.

UI / DOM ELEMENTS:
- Create a top-left title: 'Watch Configurator' in white, font-size 24px, id='title'.
- Create 4 strap-selection buttons at the bottom center of the screen in a horizontal row, each as a colored circle (40px diameter, border-radius 50%) with ids: 'btn-leather', 'btn-metal', 'btn-rubber', 'btn-nato'. Active strap button gets a white 2px border.
- Create a 'Rotate' toggle button (id='btn-rotate') at top-right that enables/disables auto-rotation of the watch (rotates around Y axis at 0.01 rad/frame).
- Create a price display (id='price-display') showing the price: Leather=$149, Metal=$299, Rubber=$99, NATO=$129. Format: '$XXX'.
- Create a strap name label (id='strap-label') showing the current strap name in uppercase.

KEYBOARD INTERACTIONS:
- Press '1','2','3','4' keys to select straps (leather, metal, rubber, nato respectively).
- Press 'R' to toggle auto-rotation.
- Press 'P' to toggle particle effects visibility (enable/disable particle bursts on swap).

STATE MANAGEMENT:
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields:
  - currentStrap: string ('leather'|'metal'|'rubber'|'nato')
  - strapIndex: number (0-3)
  - price: number (149, 299, 99, or 129)
  - autoRotate: boolean (default false)
  - particlesEnabled: boolean (default true)
  - particlesActive: boolean (true when particles are currently animating)
  - swapCount: number (how many strap swaps have been performed, starts at 0)
  - modelLoaded: boolean (true once GLB is loaded)
  - cameraDistance: number (updated each frame, camera.position.length())
  - watchRotationY: number (current Y rotation of the watch group in radians)

ANIMATION LOOP:
- Animate particles each frame if active (update positions, fade alpha).
- If autoRotate is true, rotate watch group around Y.
- Update cameraDistance and watchRotationY in __3D_STATE__ each frame.

Make sure all DOM elements have proper z-index and position:absolute/fixed styling so they overlay the 3D canvas.
physics_constraints: Particles should follow basic kinematics: position += velocity * dt, with gravity pulling particles down (y velocity -= 0.02 per frame). Particles must not produce NaN positions. Camera distance must remain positive and finite.
